title: Charles Hémard de Denonville, cardinal de Mâcon, Rome and Orvieto to Anne de Montmorency, 1536-37, in Mascon's cipher (BnF fr. 3053, DECODE R4233-R4247; BnF fr. 3071 no. 4)

transcription.notes: Line count is of cipher lines, not tokens; the readings file gives aliases per line.
About 250 cipher lines; 66 transcribed (P2, P3, P5, P6).
Two letters and a postscript in one record; read in passages (R4239.md P2-P15, R4239b.md P16-P30).

transcription.notes: About 45 lines mixed with clear text; roughly 840 cipher signs by the readers' counts (f. 9r ll. 3-25 ~190, ll. 26-34 ~190 with ~175 read, f. 9v ll. 1-16 ~463 all decoded). The alias files mix line labels, clear-text brackets and {code} groups, so no clean count was measured. Moved here from targets/gramont1529/ on 14 Oct 2026 (same key).

system.summary: Homophonic substitution on digit-like graphic signs, one sign per letter, with doubled-letter signs, nulls and three two-digit code groups.
system.sibling_key: 'Mascon's cipher' as reconstructed by S. Tomokiyo from fr. 3053 and tabulated by G. Lasry (2023) for BnF fr. 3071 f. 9; working table macon_key.md (moved here from targets/gramont1529/), used with corrections.
system.notes: Code groups 20 = l'Empereur, 30 = pape, 40 = roy, and no others in the seven fr. 3053 records or the fr. 3071 letter. The barred-cross family of signs reads F, P, O, U, V and D in the same hand and is separable only by context; the big curly X is Q/U, not N, contrary to the working table. distinct_symbols counts the fr. 3053 records. The f. 85 record (R4248) is in a second, unrelated fr. 3053 cipher and is its own entry since 14 Oct 2026 (targets/r4248/).

prior_solution.where: Contemporary marginal and interlinear decipherments of some fr. 3053 passages in the volume itself, and the slip f. 9bis deciphering the f. 9v passage of fr. 3071 no. 4. No printed or online plaintext: Tomokiyo and Lasry publish the key only. Lasry also decoded fr. 3071 no. 4 in 2023, unpublished (Lasry, 21 Sept 2026); no Lasry decipherment of the fr. 3053 letters is recorded.

texts.label: R4233, fr. 3053 f. 6 ff., Rome, 26 Jan 1536 o.s. (= 1537)
texts.summary: The cardinal de Mâcon to Montmorency: pourparlers on marriages for Pier Luigi Farnese's children, the imperial ambassador and Venice; if the French cardinals were in Rome they could steer a conclave, the pope being 'septuagenaire et plus'. He reports the mission of cardinal Verulano's secretary to Switzerland and suspects 'quelque dessaing sur le duché de Millan'. Pass 5 (shape-true re-transcription, signs and reading line by line) supersedes the earlier R4233.md.

texts.label: R4234, fr. 3053 ff. 16r-18v, Rome, Feb 1536 o.s. (= 1537)
texts.summary: Soundings on a settlement, the bishop of Lodi's view that the King should never consent, cardinal Pisani's report, the marriages of Pier Luigi Farnese's children and the match with Cosimo de' Medici, and the arming of Pier Luigi's army (Stefano Colonna for the foot, Giovanni Battista Savelli for the horse). Pass 5 supersedes the earlier pass files, also listed.

reading_review.note: Overturns the per-document C. The pass-5 running reading of ff. 16r-17v builds long French sentences (the soldiers raised for Parma and Piacenza, the Milan plan, Contarini); the [?] holes are scattered, densest on f. 16v, and f. 18r's elisions are in the clear passages, not the cipher.

texts.label: R4235, fr. 3053 f. 21 ff., Rome, 15 Feb 1536 o.s. (= 1537)
texts.summary: 'J'ay sceu de bon lieu que le dict pape vouloit entretenir le Roy de mariage', to use the King's good words with the Emperor; Mâcon begs Montmorency to tell no one but the King and to keep the envoys' charge secret, above all from the bishop of Verona (Giberti). The three contemporary marginal decipherments agree with the reading word for word.

texts.label: R4238, fr. 3053 ff. 32v-33r, Rome, [xiii?] Sept 1536
texts.summary: The bearer is sent by the Sienese exiles to press the King to an enterprise against Siena, which Mâcon sees no prospect in; a German at Rome claiming to be of Ferdinand's chamber offers to enter the King's service and gives him letters for a lansquenet captain with count Wilhelm von Fürstenberg.

texts.label: R4239, fr. 3053 ff. 35r-38v, Rome, 6 Apr 1537
texts.summary: The marriage of Ottavio Farnese to the Emperor's daughter Margaret, the intrigues of the exile cardinals Salviati and Ridolfi after Alessandro de' Medici's murder, and a bid for Pier Luigi Farnese: against the Imperialists' offer of Novara, Mâcon counters with 'quelque honneste estat en France'. Ff. 37r-v are a contemporary clear copy of letter 2 (pass5/R4239_f37_clear.md).

reading_review.note: Overturns the per-document C. Letter 2 (f. 36r-v) and the second paragraph of letter 1 (Ridolfi, the duke of Urbino) read in whole sentences; the first paragraph of letter 1 is summarised with elisions and f. 38r ll. 5-14 are read only in part (listed as gaps).

texts.label: R4240, fr. 3053 f. 40r-v, Orvieto, 2 Sept 1536
texts.summary: The general council: Vergerio carried word to the Germans that they might come and speak as the Holy Spirit inspired them; the pope, judging this 'la totale ruine de l'Eglise', has sent an auditor to summon them on the old custom instead, and the Germans say pope, cardinals and bishops must first be reformed.

texts.label: R4247 letter 1, fr. 3053 f. 77r-v, Orvieto, [early Sept] 1536
texts.summary: Andrea Doria and Milan: Mâcon infers from Doria's letter to the conte dell'Anguillara a secret treaty between the pope and the Emperor and puts it to Paul III; then cardinal Filonardi's man sounds him on Milan passing to Pier Luigi Farnese's son or the young Sforza, and Mâcon answers that the King will never consent, Milan 'estant leur vray heritage'.

texts.label: R4247 letter 2, fr. 3053 f. 78v, Orvieto, 1 Sept 1536
texts.summary: The second letter of the record, signed by Mâcon at Orvieto on 1 September 1536; it ends 'il seroit icy fort difficille de recouvrer gens de cheval ne artillerie; bien trouverroit on tant de gens de pied, et bons, qu'on vouldroit, et beaucoup de gentilz homes forussiz'.

texts.label: BnF fr. 3071 no. 4, ff. 9-10 and slip f. 9bis, Rome, 11 Apr 1537
texts.summary: Mâcon to Montmorency, 11 April 1537: the Farnese marriage offer (Vittoria Farnese to Cosimo de' Medici) and Paul III's threat, relayed through Latino Giovenale, to declare for the Emperor if it is refused; Pier Luigi Farnese and Novara; the King's Turkish alliance 'se verifie clerement'. The slip f. 9bis is a contemporary decipherment of the f. 9v passage, matched almost word for word. Lasry decoded this letter in 2023 but never published it.

reading_review.note: fr3071_no4/macon1537_reading.md assembles the letter for the first time: cipher from the glyph decodes of the two Sept passes (Lasry's 2023 table), f. 9v ll. 4-16 checked against the contemporary decipherment on the slip f. 9bis (transcribed in full, macon1537_slip_f9bis.txt; agrees except car/ce que and peine/peur, where the figures are followed); clear text re-read on the Gallica images (f. 9v Mantua passage and f. 10r close for the first time; the count is Cifuentes). Reading body 0.676 (46/68) plain, 0.868 explicit holes; look-alike letters about 0.3%. Open: five short cipher spots on f. 9r and single doubtful clear words (illegible).
